The Little Fox That Lives On My Bookshelf — Free Pattern

I wanted a fox that looks like he just came in from the woods — orange all over, white belly, white tip on the tail, and those pointy ears with white inside.

He's about 6 inches tall when he sits, which is my favorite size for gifting. I made this one twice because the first tail was too thin. Second time I brushed it out and now it poofs like a real fox tail. My notes below are exactly how I make him now.

Skill level Beginner friendly — magic ring, sc, inc, dec
Hook 4.0mm + chunky orange, white, black for nose
Size ~6" sitting, ~4" wide — 2.5 hour make

Why this fox is different from my other animals

Most of my little animals have round heads. Foxes don't. They have that long snout that makes them look clever. So for this one I crochet the head round, then I add a separate snout that sticks out — it gives him that proper fox profile instead of looking like a cat in orange.

I also learned — after trying to change colors mid-round for the belly — that sewing the white belly on as a separate oval is so much cleaner. No jog, no yarn carrying up the side. It sits flat and it looks intentional, like his winter coat.

He lives on my bookshelf now between two little pine cones I collected last fall. My son keeps trying to steal him.

Your yarn basket — what I actually used

  • Yarn: Chunky cotton — Burnt orange ~100g (Hobbii Sultan #15), White ~30g, Black scrap for nose
  • Hook: 4.0mm. If you can see stuffing, go to 3.5mm
  • Eyes: 12mm safety eyes — placed between Rounds 11 and 12, 7 stitches apart. Mark with pins first, snap after you like it
  • Extras: Polyfill, tapestry needle, stitch markers, small scissors, optional wire brush for tail
My tension is quite tight. If yours is looser, he'll be a little bigger — that's fine, just keep it consistent so his head and body match.

Starting the head — magic ring and first increases, orange yarn with my 4.0mm hook.

Size and gauge

Mine is 6" tall sitting, head about 3.25" wide. With DK and 3.5mm hook, about 4.5". With super bulky and 5.5mm, about 7" and very huggable.

Abbreviations

mr — magic ring, ch — chain, sc — single crochet, inc — 2 sc in same stitch, dec — invisible decrease (front loops only), FO — fasten off, [...] x6 — repeat. I work in spiral, marker moves up each round.

Roadmap

My order:
1. Head — round base 6→36
2. Snout — white-tipped long nose
3. Ears — orange outer + white inner
4. Body — orange tube + separate white belly oval
5. Tail — orange with white tip, brushed
6. Arms x2 + Legs x2 — all orange

Step 1: Head + snout — the foxy face

STEP 1 · HEAD & SNOUT
Head — orange:
R1: mr, 6 sc (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3: [sc 1, inc] x6 (18)
R4: [sc 2, inc] x6 (24)
R5: [sc 3, inc] x6 (30)
R6: [sc 4, inc] x6 (36)
R7-R11: sc around 36 — 5 rounds even (36)
Place eyes between R11 and R12, 7 sts apart. Pin first, check straight on.
R12-R14: sc around 36 — 3 rounds (36)
R15: [sc 4, dec] x6 (30)
R16: [sc 3, dec] x6 (24) — start stuffing, firm
R17: [sc 2, dec] x6 (18)
R18: [sc 1, dec] x6 (12)
R19: dec x6 (6) — close

Snout — start white tip, then orange:
White R1: mr, 4 sc (4)
R2: [sc 1, inc] x2 (6)
R3: sc 6 — white
Switch orange R4: [sc 2, inc] x2 (8)
R5: [sc 3, inc] x2 (10)
R6-R7: sc 10 — 2 rounds
FO, leave tail, stuff lightly. Sew centered between eyes, bottom edge at about R14 of head. Embroider small black nose on white tip.

Head after even rounds — eyes pinned between R11-R12 before I snap them in. Snout still separate here.

Step 2: Ears with white inners

STEP 2 · EARS
Inner ear — white, make 2:
R1: mr, 4 sc (4)
R2: [sc 1, inc] x2 (6)
R3: [sc 2, inc] x2 (8)
FO white.

Outer ear — orange, make 2:
R1: mr, 4 sc (4)
R2: [sc 1, inc] x2 (6)
R3: [sc 2, inc] x2 (8)
R4: [sc 3, inc] x2 (10)
R5: [sc 4, inc] x2 (12)
Place white inner on orange outer, sc around through both layers with orange — 12 sc — gives clean white center. FO, leave tail, flatten.

I sew ears between Rounds 3-7 of head, about 8 stitches apart inside edges, slightly forward. Don't stuff them — they stand up better flat.

Step 3: Body with separate white belly

STEP 3 · BODY
Body — orange:
R1: mr, 6 (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3: [sc 1, inc] x6 (18)
R4: [sc 2, inc] x6 (24)
R5: [sc 3, inc] x6 (30)
R6-R12: sc 30 — 7 rounds straight
R13: [sc 3, dec] x6 (24)
R14-R16: sc 24 — 3 rounds
FO, leave long tail, stuff firm.

White belly oval:
Ch 9, sc in 2nd ch, sc 6, 3 sc in last, turn, sc 6, inc (18)
R2: inc, sc 6, inc x3, sc 6, inc x2 (24)
R3: inc, sc 7, [inc, sc 1] x3, sc 6, [inc, sc 1] x2 (30)
R4: sc 30 — FO, leave tail. Sew to front center of body with white yarn.

Body with belly panel — I sew the white oval on first with white yarn so you don't see the stitches from the front.

Step 4: Tail — the fluffy one

STEP 4 · TAIL
Tail — start white, then orange:
White R1: mr, 6 (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3-R4: sc 12 — 2 rounds white
Switch orange R5: sc 12
R6: [sc 1, inc] x6 (18)
R7-R12: sc 18 — 6 rounds
R13: [sc 1, dec] x6 (12)
R14: dec x6 (6) — FO, stuff lightly, leave tail.

After stuffing, I take a clean slicker brush and gently brush the orange part outward — not the white tip. It makes it fluff out like a real fox tail. If you don't have a brush, just pick the yarn loops with your needle.

Step 5: Arms and legs

STEP 5 · LIMBS
Arms — make 2 in orange:
R1: mr, 6 (6)
R2: [sc 1, inc] x3 (9)
R3-R10: sc 9 — 8 rounds
FO, leave tail, lightly stuff hand only.

Legs — make 2 in orange:
R1: mr, 6 (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3-R12: sc 12 — 10 rounds
FO, stuff, flatten bottom.

Step 6: Assembly — so he sits nice and straight

STEP 6 · PUTTING TOGETHER

Pin first, sew second. I always do that now after sewing a head on crooked once and having to rip it.

  • Head to body — centered, whip stitch twice around. No wobble.
  • Snout already on head — give it a little push up so it points forward, not down.
  • Ears — already placed, but reinforce with one more stitch through both layers.
  • Arms at sides, at Rounds 5-6 of body, angled slightly forward.
  • Legs at bottom front, flat base so he sits. Move back one round if he tips.
  • Tail at back center, at about Rounds 6-7 of body — sew securely, it’s heavy when brushed.

All my pieces before final sewing — head with snout, ears with white centers, body with white belly, tail with white tip, arms and legs.

My little finishing touches

I weave all tails inside and pop the knots into the stuffing. Invisible decreases only — front loops — so no holes. I use a black embroidery thread for tiny whisker dots on the snout — just two small french knots each side, optional. And I lightly brush the tail once more after assembly.
